source.title: Beyond the storage capacity: data driven satisfiability transition
source.authors: P. Rotondo; Mauro Pastore; M. Gherardi

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: Analyzes random-label satisfiability for margin classifiers with an analytical synaptic-volume method, rather than training standard deep networks with stochastic gradient methods.
record.gate_note: The paper’s own random-label margin analysis bears on V1. Its discussion of deep-network generalization and cited work is not an experimental result. It does not report training-time comparisons, unstructured-input training, label-noise sweeps, regularization tests, or learning order.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes expressivity and satisfiability in kernel and margin classifiers. Its integrated synaptic volume sums over labelings; it does not measure standard deep networks learning a fixed random labeling with stochastic gradient methods. None of V1–V6 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors identify a data-driven transition in simple classifiers, argue for data-dependent complexity measures beyond storage capacity, and leave extension to deep neural networks for future work.
record.recipe_differences: Analytical combinatorial and annealed synaptic-volume calculations for kernel and margin classifiers; no deep-network training procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The random-label margin threshold depends on margin κ; the paper states that it diverges as κ → 0 and tends to 0 as κ → ∞.

fits_no_version.finding: For margin classifiers, the annealed integrated synaptic volume shrinks exponentially above the margin-dependent load in Equation (7); this threshold diverges as the margin approaches zero and approaches zero as the margin increases without bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Margin constraints produce a transition in an integrated measure of classifier expressivity, even for unstructured data.

record.problems: The random-label result is analytical and uses an annealed approximation; the reported synaptic volume is a proxy, not a direct training-error measurement. The authors state that addressing deep neural networks is future work.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting by standard deep networks using stochastic gradient methods, near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence slowdown with increasing label corruption.
Perfect fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily increasing test error across a label-corruption sweep.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Unstructured data in this paper does not mean the shuffled-pixel or Gaussian-noise training conditions in V3. The structured-data VC-entropy results also do not test any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test standard deep networks, stochastic-gradient training, or observed training error. The random-label analysis is for margin classifiers and uses an annealed synaptic-volume proxy.

rows.subject: kernel architecture
rows.operation_detail: Computed the annealed synaptic volume for margin classification of randomly labelled, unstructured data.
rows.measure: Critical load α∗M(κ) above which the synaptic volume shrinks exponentially fast in n.
rows.locator: Section “Margin-driven transition with unstructured data,” Eq. (7)
rows.note: The authors describe the synaptic volume as a probe into the phase transition; it is not a measured training error or a training run.
rows.check: Equation (7) and its limiting behavior are correctly transcribed, but the subject should be a margin classifier analyzed through an annealed integrated synaptic volume. This volume is analogous to Equation (5), which integrates over labels, and its exponential shrinkage does not establish training error on a fixed random labeling. It cannot determine V1.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
